refined_claim_text: [ASSUMED-N]: The global market for high-value cargo escort services is sometimes cited at ~$21B (2024); no credible primary source supports this specific figure. The nearest credible comparable — global cash-in-transit / secure logistics — is sized by independent analysts at $7.9–$47.6B depending on scope definition, with APAC representing 31–38% of the broader secure logistics market (~$15–18B APAC across all secure logistics sub-segments). The $21.3B DataIntelo figure for the narrow 'high-value cargo escort' sub-segment cannot be validated.

primary_sources_found.key_data: US armored transportation services market size: $4.3B in 2025 / grew 1.2% in 2024. US-only, not global, and covers all armored transport not just high-value cargo escort.
primary_sources_found.note: IBISWorld is paywalled; figure extracted from public statistics page. Global extrapolation not possible from this alone.

primary_sources_found.key_data: Global secure logistics market valued at USD 47.62B in 2025; APAC holds 31.6% share (~$15.1B). This is the broader secure logistics category including cash management, ATM replenishment, and high-value goods transport — not specifically cargo escort.
primary_sources_found.note: Mordor Intelligence discloses structured methodology (BIS data, customs manifests, company filings, primary interviews). Higher confidence than DataIntelo aggregators but scope is broader than the claim.

primary_sources_found.key_data: Global cash-in-transit market: USD 7.9B in 2025 (narrow CIT-only scope); APAC fastest-growing at 5.3% CAGR. Key players: Brink's, Loomis, GardaWorld, Prosegur, Allied Universal.
primary_sources_found.note: Narrow CIT-only definition. $21.3B DataIntelo figure does not align with this scoping.

primary_sources_found.key_data: Brink's FY2024 total revenue: $5.01B. By geography: North America $1.65B, Latin America $1.31B, Europe $1.23B, Rest of World $823M. No cargo escort sub-segment disclosed separately; CVM (Cash & Valuables Management) is largest segment at ~72% of revenue (~$3.6B). BGS (Brink's Global Services, the high-value cargo arm) is not broken out as a standalone line.
primary_sources_found.note: Useful for bottom-up triangulation: if Brink's is ~15-20% of global secure logistics, implies global market ~$25-33B — consistent with Mordor's broader figure but not with DataIntelo's narrow $21.3B cargo escort claim.

primary_sources_found.key_data: Prosegur FY2024 total sales: €4.91B. Prosegur Cash (valuables logistics): €2.09B. No cargo escort sub-segment broken out. Geographic APAC data not disclosed at sub-segment level.
primary_sources_found.note: Confirms Prosegur Cash is ~$2.2B equivalent — consistent with the market being spread across multiple large players, none individually approaching $21B.

primary_sources_found.key_data: Loomis FY2024 revenue: SEK 30,442M (~USD 2.8B at 2024 average rate). CIT + CMS = 62% of segment revenue. Asia presence is limited (Hong Kong, Dubai, Shanghai) — not a major APAC player.
primary_sources_found.note: Third-largest global CIT player confirms market is fragmented; APAC is not a primary region for Loomis.

notes: The $21.3B DataIntelo figure for 'global high-value cargo escort services' is unsupported by any credible primary source. DataIntelo is a known aggregator with no disclosed methodology, primary data collection, or auditable inputs — it cannot serve as a market anchor in external pitch materials. Three independent analytical findings follow: (1) The nearest credible adjacent market, global cash-in-transit (narrow definition), is sized at ~$7.9B by Expert Market Research or ~$16.8B by Cognitive Market Research in 2024 — both materially different from $21.3B. (2) The broader 'secure logistics' market (which includes CIT, ATM services, high-value goods transport, and related) is sized at $47.6B globally by Mordor Intelligence with disclosed methodology, APAC at ~31.6% share (~$15B). (3) Bottom-up triangulation from the four largest operators (Brink's ~$5B, Prosegur Cash ~$2.2B, GardaWorld ~$5.8B guidance, Loomis ~$2.8B) already accounts for ~$15-16B combined revenue for just the top four — implying a $21.3B global 'cargo escort' sub-segment would require these players to derive nearly 100% of revenue from that one sub-service, which contradicts their disclosed segment structures. Recommended revision: replace DataIntelo anchor with Mordor Intelligence secure logistics figure ($47.6B global / ~$15B APAC) with a note that 'high-value cargo escort is a sub-segment of secure logistics; standalone sizing is not available from credible sources.' If the claim is load-bearing for a pitch, it must be field-validated or dropped.
